topology: 2 nodes x 4 H100, 8 MPI ranks = 7 PP + 1 PME, benchRIB (2,136,412 atoms), Open MPI 4.1.5 over UCX 1.15 (HPC-X 2.16) over NDR InfiniBand. Captured at BOTH the public UCP doors and the uct_iface_ops_t transport table, so that the shared-memory half of a real domain decomposition is visible for the first time.
golden: none - assertions only. Every claim is derived from GROMACS's decomposition (npp, npme, dd_x, ranks_per_node), from GROMACS's own MPI tag enum, or from Open MPI's UCP tag encoding. Nothing is derived from a capture.
workload_note:
ROUND 2. Round 1 (REPORT.md) judged this application against comm_edges and the raw UCX tables and found comm_edges structurally empty on the HPC-X stack. Round 2 aims at the layer that replaces it: ucx_deep, and the derived transport_mix / tag_flow / tag_recv_resolved built on top of it. The oracle is stated in full in PREDICTION.md, committed before this run existed.

WHERE EVERY PARAMETER COMES FROM.

* npp/npme: `-npme 1` of 8 ranks. domdec/domdec.cpp:552 dd_interleaved_pme_ranks over :540 ddindex2pmeindex places the single PME rank at world rank 7 and makes DD cell index equal MPI rank, under BOTH -ddorder interleave (the default) and pp_pme.
* dd_x: `-dd 7 1 1`. 7 is prime so nx*ny*nz=7 admits only a permutation of 7x1x1 anyway.
* pulses_x: predicted 1, from domdec/domdec.cpp:2326, printed as `The initial number of communication pulses is: X 1` because -dlb no takes the non-DLB branch. A cell is ~3.9 nm against a pair-list radius under 1.5 nm. IF THE LOG SAYS 2, the halo partner set becomes (x+-1),(x+-2) and every edge count below is void; the job script prints the line.
* ranks_per_node: `mpirun --map-by ppr:4:node`, so ranks 0-3 on node A and 4-7 on node B.
* natoms: byte offset 72 of benchRIB.tpr, big-endian uint32 (round 1's NOTES.md). Read from the input file, never from a capture.
* rvec_bytes / real_bytes: sizeof(rvec) = 3 x float and sizeof(real) = float, because the build is mixed precision -- `Precision: mixed` in GROMACS's own log header, read from the log and not assumed. In a double build they would be 24 and 8 and every volume below would double. real_bytes is here only because round 1's asserts/pme_coord_volume.sql needs it for the PP_PME_CHARGE term; nothing in asserts-r2/ uses either.
* ompi_*: ompi/mca/pml/ucx/pml_ucx_request.h:34-44 in Open MPI v4.1.x. PML_UCX_TAG_BITS 24 / RANK_BITS 20 / CONTEXT_BITS 20, so a UCP tag is (mpi_tag << 40) | (my_rank << 20) | context_id. PML_UCX_TAG_GET_SOURCE(:65) is exactly ((tag >> 20) & 0xFFFFF). An MPI_ANY_SOURCE receive decodes to 0xFFFFF = 1048575, which is not a valid rank and is therefore self-excluding - no mask test is needed.
* gmx_tag_*: ewald/pme_pp_communication.h:54 (eCommType_COORD = 7, eCommType_COORD_GPU = 8) and domdec/haloexchange.h:74 (HaloMpiTag::X = 0, ::F = 1).
* fabric_pct_lo/hi: the DD's own bound. Of the 7 PME spokes 4 cross the node boundary and of the 7 halo edges 2 do, so the fabric's share of application bytes lies strictly between 2/7 = 28.6% and 4/7 = 57.1% for ANY relative weight of halo and PME. Widened to [25,60] for wireup and collectives. NO MEASUREMENT ENTERS THIS BOUND.
* interior_fabric_max_pct / exterior_fabric_min_pct: rank 5's partners are 4, 6 and the PME rank 7, all on node B, so it has no cross-node partner at all and its fabric share should be collective residue only. The assertions DERIVE that rank from npp and ranks_per_node rather than naming it, so no rank number the run produced appears in any query.

nsteps IS 200, NOT ROUND 1's 1000, and deliberately. ucx_deep records one row per WIRE operation, and an intra-node rendezvous that fragments in the shared-memory transport could produce two orders of magnitude more rows than ucx_tag_send did at 1000 steps. Every oracle in asserts-r2/ is a ratio or a set, never an absolute count, so the step count enters none of THEM.

IT DOES ENTER THE ROUND-1 ASSERTIONS, WHICH THIS JOB ALSO RUNS, and the first edition of this note said otherwise. job-r2.sbatch re-runs asserts/*.sql over the CSV export to show the round-2 capture has not regressed round 1's result, and two of those -- pme_coord_volume and pme_rank_force_volume -- are absolute byte volumes of the form rvec_bytes * natoms * (nsteps+1). On job 45235734 they were evaluated against meta.json's nsteps=1000 and both reported the capture at 20 % of expected: 1000/200 = 5, in two independent assertions, which is the signature of a stale oracle rather than a lossy tracer. The capture was right. At nsteps=200 the same queries give 12 * 2136412 * 201 = 5,153,025,744 B against an observed 5,153,056,388 B -- 6 parts per million -- and GROMACS's own log agrees ('Statistics over 201 steps'). asserts.sh now takes ASSERT_META and job-r2.sbatch points it here, and the job script reads NSTEPS out of this file rather than carrying its own copy, so there is one step count for the run and not two.

THE tm VARIANT IS A SEPARATE EXPERIMENT AND A SHORT ONE. uct_send.tag is written only by the hardware-tag-matching doors, and MN5's HPC-X does not enable ConnectX tag offload by default, so tag_flow is predicted to hold no matched flow in the two main arms. The tm arm sets UCX_RC_MLX5_TM_ENABLE=y and UCX_TM_THRESH below GROMACS's message sizes so that the doors CAN fire; it is what tells 'the join is wrong' apart from 'the fabric was not asked'.

NO ASSERTION COUNTS MESSAGES. One MPI_Isend is not one ucp_tag_send and one ucp_tag_send is emphatically not one uct_send - that is the entire point of having both layers. Round 1 already placed the byte volume to four parts per million with ucx_tag_send alone and there is no reason to repeat it.

expect_fail_asserts.entity_close_accounted: Carried unchanged from meta.json, because asserts.sh now reads its markers from THIS file when job-r2.sbatch runs the round-1 assertions, and dropping the marker would turn a known, re-measured, correct-behaviour finding back into a red assertion. Re-measured on job 45103152 and reproduced on 45235734: what fires is clause 3, 'entity opened and never closed' -- a handful of lifetimes still live at exit, evenly spread over all 8 ranks, which suite/asserts/entity_close_accounted.sql itself calls legal and asks to be scoped per case rather than globally exempted. Unmatched closes are zero.
expect_fail_asserts.mem_owner_unambiguous: Carried unchanged from meta.json. The flagged pairs PARTIALLY OVERLAP by exactly 16 bytes, so neither contains the other and no rule picks a winner without inventing one -- which is what the assertion exists to say. Zero rows with devices > 1. The finding is about UCX's registration cache, not about comshu. Reports [skip] under -p ucx,ucx_deep since mem_owner is empty; the marker is here for the arms that do populate it.
expect_fail_asserts.expect_fail_note: These two are statements about the stack, not about the round, so they belong to both meta files. If a future round makes either pass, asserts.sh reports [XPASS] and the marker should be removed rather than kept.
